title: "Overview of Ecosystem Service: Local Climate Regulation"
format:

    embed-resources: true
    standalone: true

Local climate regulation is urban cooling. Vegetation lowers city temperatures, buildings spend
less electricity on air conditioning, and the account values that saved electricity. The base year
is 2019 and the price convention recorded in `es_config.csv` is `avoided energy cost`. The account
follows Libby Kula's approach, adopted by Chiara on 29 October 2026 in place of the CAS method.

## Sources

- Method: `Local_Climate_Regulation.docx` in the shared folder of current write-ups (Libby Kula,
  Liaila Tajibaeva, Haku Bo, Nfamara K Dampha), version of 30 October 2026, 19:02 UTC, with no
  tracked changes or comments. It replaces the appendix of 21 October 2026.
- Additional documentation: `Local_Climate_Regulation_Additional_documentation_10_7_26`, version
  of 30 October 2026, 19:00 UTC: the countries missing or zero and a country results table.
- Code: `libby-07/urban-cooling`, main `362f177` (31 October 2025), the registered repository.
- Result: `local_climate_regulation_gep.csv` of 13 July 2026, the code register's results file.
  The staged copy is byte-identical to it (sha256 `8c92bd10...f9ac`).

## Quantity

The write-up covers about 46,000 of the 123,034 urban areas in the Global Urban Polygons and
Points Dataset, those large enough for the 1 km air-temperature input (GSHTD monthly means). For
each urban area and month, the hottest pixel stands for the temperature without nature, and the
cooling of each pixel is the difference from it, with a 70°F threshold. The write-up then
describes the savings per 100 m pixel, referring to Urban InVEST cooling results, and per 1 km
pixel resampled to the population grid. Which resolution the delivered values come from is not
established.

The cooling is converted into fewer cooling degree-days and then into electricity saved per
person. The write-up derives the electricity per degree-day from a regression across countries,
while the delivered final applies each country's own cooling consumption per degree-day (below).

## Price

The World Bank (2020) electricity price for each country, in 2019 US dollars per kilowatt-hour.

## Valuation

Savings are the electricity saved per person times population times the national price, summed
over the pixels of each urban area and then over the urban areas of a country. In the city-month
files the identity is

$$
\text{total\_savings\_usd} = \text{kwh\_diff} \times \text{price\_usd\_per\_kwh}
$$

and `city_savings_identity` recomputes it at rtol 1e-6 and raises if it breaks.

The December 2025 version of the results is exactly the sum of those city files. They carry a
single global slope of electricity per degree-day. The delivered final of 13 July 2026 divides that
slope out and applies each country's own cooling consumption per degree-day:

$$
\text{final} = \frac{\text{December 2025 value}}{\text{URBAN\_COOLING\_OLD\_GLOBAL\_MC}} \times \text{consumption per degree-day}
$$

`apply_country_marginal_consumption` holds that step. The registered code applies it only to an
older 55-country table, and the code and inputs that produced the final are not yet in hand.

## What the library reports

`gep_calculation` imports Libby Kula's delivered final, parses its dollar-formatted column through
`parse_dollar_column`, and joins it onto the account's 250 countries by label. The final is
imported, not recomputed. Two comparison columns sit beside it: the December 2025 city sums
(`local_climate_regulation_gep_city_sum_lineage`) and the CAS 2019 results
(`local_climate_regulation_gep_cas`), which the code register names as the cross-check.

## Coverage

The published table is one row for each of the account's 250 countries, base year 2019, in
constant 2019 USD, and it is the delivered final as imported: 174 countries carry a value, none
is zero, and 76 are missing. The delivered total is $14,188,882,295.

The 30 October additional documentation accounts for the 76 differently. It values five of them,
Côte d'Ivoire $49,400, Eritrea $2,953.04, São Tomé and Príncipe $114, South Sudan $1,455 and Yemen
$561 ($54,483.04 in all), and its country table otherwise equals the final in the 174 countries
both value (joined on country keys). It lists 26 as true zeros: Iceland, below the threshold in
every month, and 25 places without an urban area in its source, 24 of which it also lists as
lacking price or consumption data. The other 45 it lists as missing price, consumption or
temperature data, or as unsure. The library keeps the final as delivered, so these five values
and 26 zeros are not in the account.

## Inputs

From `es_parameters.csv`, scoped to the `local_climate_regulation` service:

- `local_climate_regulation_final_path`, Libby Kula's delivered final, the reported value.
- `local_climate_regulation_city_savings_path`, the December 2025 city-month files.
- `local_climate_regulation_cas_results_path`, the CAS 2019 country results, for comparison only.

## Output

`gep_calculation` writes `gep_by_country_base_year.csv` into its own task directory, holding the
r250 identifiers and attributes, `year`, `local_climate_regulation_gep` and the two comparison
columns.

## Method constants

- `URBAN_COOLING_OLD_GLOBAL_MC = 1.71737465916468`, the global slope the final divides out.
- `URBAN_COOLING_CDD_BASE_C = 18.0` and `URBAN_COOLING_SMOOTH_WINDOW_C = 1.0`, used by the helper
  `temp_degc_to_cdd_smooth`. That helper is not the authors' degree-day curve, which in their code
  is a Fahrenheit polynomial switching at 70°F, the threshold the 30 October write-up states. It
  does not enter the reported value.

## Taken as given

The cooling estimates behind the city files, the national electricity prices and the delivered
final.

## What is open

- The provenance of the final's last step: its code, the IEA-CMCC 2019 cooling degree-day file,
  the per-country consumption per degree-day, and which energy-share version was used. The 30
  October documents do not supply them, so the final is imported, not reproduced.
- The write-up and the delivered values still differ: the gradient is a regression in the
  write-up and each country's own ratio in the final, the resolution is described both as 100 m
  and as 1 km, and the additional documentation's five values and 26 true zeros (Iceland among
  them) are missing in the final. The threshold is settled: the write-up states 70°F, the code's.
- Review comments raised on the 21 October appendix: the treatment of places without air
  conditioning, the model inputs, the urban-area size criterion shared with other urban services.
  The 30 October write-up carries no comments, and these points are not yet checked against it.
